The ending of the story feels entirely natural and earned, bringing all the central character arcs, themes, and motifs to a satisfying resolution. The narrative resolves the core conflict between Denise and Miss Emily through mutual respect (via the velouté recipe and the subsequent business venture) and sees Daniel finally build the house he had only been sketching for years. Furthermore, the final scene brings the story full circle by returning to the Price King and the motif of the "single shallot" that originally brought Denise and Daniel together. By contrasting her current happiness with the loneliness the shallot once represented, and by tying back to earlier details like the "tear under the arm" and the "windows tall as doors," the conclusion provides a strong, purposeful sense of closure.
